glosses: Actuality.

glosses: Something done once and for all, as distinguished from a work.
A product of a legislative body, a statute.

examples.text: But was it responsible governance to pass the Longitude Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.

glosses: (In the United States) A legislative proposal, a bill that has not yet become law.

examples.text: Under current law, employers can drag out the union election process... Under the PRO Act, workers and the NLRB set union election procedures. The employer is not involved.

glosses: To perform a theatrical role.

examples.text: I started acting at the age of eleven in my local theatre.

glosses: Of a play: to be acted out (well or badly).

examples.text: But whatever types he assumes, the need to have a good play which acts delightfully well before the audience, and to their delectation, is the dominant thrust. If the play acts well, the director gets the credits.

glosses: To behave in a certain manner for an indefinite length of time.

examples.text: A dog which acts aggressively is likely to bite.
I believe that Bill’s stuck-up because of the way that he acts.
He’s acting strangely—I think there’s something wrong with him.

glosses: To convey an appearance of being.

examples.text: He acted unconcerned so the others wouldn’t worry.

glosses: To do something that causes a change binding on the doer.

examples.text: act on behalf of John

glosses: To have an effect (on).

examples.text: High-pressure oxygen acts on the central nervous system and may cause convulsions or death.

glosses: To play (a role).

examples.text: He’s been acting Shakespearean leads since he was twelve.

glosses: To feign.

examples.text: He acted the angry parent, but was secretly amused.
With acted fear the villain thus pursued.

glosses: To carry out work as a legal representative in relation to a particular legal matter.

examples.text: A lawyer cannot act until they have been formally instructed by their client.

glosses: To possess an action onto (some other structure). Examples include the group action of a group on a set, the action of a ring on a module by scalar multiplication, and the action of a group or algebra on a vector space via a representation.

examples.text: This group acts on the circle, so it can't be left-orderable!

glosses: To move to action; to actuate; to animate.

examples.text: Self-love, the spring of motion, acts the soul.
